R0137.title: Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) Fraud
R0137.definition: Fraudulently consuming BNPL credit limits and refusing to repay, or exploiting audit loopholes in BNPL mechanisms to obtain goods and funds fraudulently.
R0137.description: BNPL fraud targets the BNPL credit consumption model, manifesting domestically primarily as abuse of credit payment tools such as Huabei and Baitiao. Main fraud patterns include: (1) Fake identity applications: using synthetic identities or stolen identities to activate BNPL limits for malicious consumption. (2) Cash-out fraud: converting BNPL limits into cash through fake transactions with no intention to repay. (3) Multi-platform loan fraud: simultaneously applying for limits on multiple BNPL platforms, concentrating consumption then defaulting. (4) Refund fraud: initiating refunds after receiving goods while retaining the items. (5) Account takeover: stealing others' accounts and using their BNPL limits for consumption. (6) Merchant collusion: colluding with fake merchants to create fake transactions to extract BNPL funds.
R0137.influence: Causes credit losses for platforms and financial institutions, rising bad debt rates, and impacts the sustainable development of BNPL business.

references.title: Huabei/Baitiao Cash-Out Risk Prevention and Control

observables: After a BNPL limit is activated, consumption is concentrated to the credit ceiling within a short window, with merchants highly concentrated in cash-out categories
The same device or receiving merchant is linked to multiple BNPL transactions, with amounts near the credit ceiling and abnormal frequency
Borrowers activate limits and concentrate consumption on multiple BNPL platforms in near-synchrony, then become unreachable or default shortly after loan disbursement
A refund is initiated shortly after a BNPL transaction is completed, but the goods are not actually returned or the refund flows to an anomalous account
